title: Hunnic Empire
capsule: Under Rugila, and then his nephews Bleda and Attila (r. 434-453), the Huns forged a vast steppe empire stretching from the Rhine to the Caspian, extracting tribute from both Roman empires and campaigning as far as Gaul and Italy. Attila's death in 453 triggered a Germanic revolt led by the Gepid king Ardaric that shattered centralized Hunnic rule at the Battle of Nedao (454). Fragmentary successor groups, the Kutrigur and Utigur Huns and allied Hunno-Bulgar tribes, persisted on the Pontic steppe for another two centuries until absorbed by the Avars and emerging Bulgar polities in the later 7th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Hunnic territorial extent is highly conjectural; the western empire's core in Pannonia is well-supported by Roman sources, but steppe frontiers from the Caspian to the Danube reflect scholarly inference from narrative sources rather than administrative records. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: medium).
